channel.title: WSJ | World
channel.description: WSJ World News RSS, without Opinions

item.title: Iran-Backed Militants Are Tightening the Screws on Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince
item.description: Mohammed bin Salman is now caught by an economy weakened by heavy spending and miscalculations of the Houthi threat.

item.title: Oil Prices Fall as Traders Weigh Russian Diesel Deal, Middle East Supply Risks
item.description: Oil fell as traders weighed prospects for increased Russian diesel supplies and a potential Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire against persistent Middle East supply risks.

item.title: U.K. Government Faces Test of Budget Credibility
item.description: The government presents its annual budget later this month, but might find it difficult to reassure bond investors that it can lower its debts.

item.title: Why China Doesn’t Want to Join the Ranks of the World’s Developed Countries
item.description: The nation is nearing high-income status, a clash with its image as a champion of the Global South.

item.title: The Welfare State Is Crushing Britain
item.description: The U.K.’s welfare bill has ballooned, its borrowing costs are now higher than any G-7 nation and it’s paying more for its debt than even spendthrift France.

item.title: Trump Pushes Russia-Ukraine Energy Ceasefire as Export Deal Draws Criticism
item.description: A bipartisan group of senators is challenging his move to allow Russia to ship diesel to the U.S., citing a 2022 law.

item.title: Houthis and Ukraine Put Trump in Treacherous Territory
item.description: The spiraling global energy mess is ensnaring more countries, and it isn’t helping Republican candidates.

item.title: Air Travel Emerges as Dangerous Front Line in Global Conflicts
item.description: Commercial air travel has been dragged into escalating conflicts, with airports, planes and airspace becoming the deliberate target of missile and drone attacks.

item.title: The Virtually Unknown Donors Powering the Rise of the New Left
item.description: Plus, how everyday cameras are being hacked for war, and the wearable way to get a blood-pressure reading.

item.title: Kenyan Club Rejects Bid to Allow Women Into Men’s Bar From ‘Out of Africa’
item.description: The elite Muthaiga Country Club’s Members Bar has long banned women and will continue to do so after a heated campaign.

item.title: India Locks Down Heart of Capital to Thwart Voter Rights Protest
item.description: The anger over the voting lists has melded with grievances from young Indians struggling to find work.

item.title: The Cameras Designed to Keep Us Safe Are Now Being Used in War
item.description: Plus, Saudi Arabia closes Riyadh’s international airport after Houthi attack, and the wave of unknown donors powering the rise of the new left.

item.title: Starving Ukrainians Are Risking Death to Escape Their Front-Line Town
item.description: All year, food supplies have dwindled as mines and drones made the road increasingly impassable.

item.title: Video Cameras Are Everywhere—and Now They Are Being Hacked for War
item.description: The highly vulnerable devices have turned into tools for combatants to track, surveil and attack the enemy.

item.title: At Least 12 Killed, Hundreds Injured at Saudi Airport in Houthi Strikes
item.description: The missiles strikes forced authorities to close Saudi Arabia’s international airport in what was the deadliest attack in the kingdom in more than a decade.

item.title: Trump Calls On Ukraine to Stop Hitting Russian Refineries—and Replace Zelensky
item.description: The clash marks a new low point in White House relations with Kyiv as Russia escalates its bombing of Ukrainian cities.

item.title: The Nordic Formula for Prospering in a Dangerous, Fragmented World
item.description: Sweden and Denmark are pouring money into defense, tightening ties with each other and Europe—and moving beyond the U.S. It’s paying off.

item.title: Houthis Bombard Saudi Air Links in Effort to Cut Kingdom Off From Rest of World
item.description: Missile attacks on airports are spooking travelers and threatening another pillar of the kingdom’s growth.

item.title: Trump Strikes Deal With Putin for Russian Diesel
item.description: The president said Russia agreed to supply large amounts of the refined fuel, marking a major policy shift that eases U.S. pressure on Moscow in hopes of lowering fuel prices ahead of the midterm elections.

item.title: Venezuela Wants to Return to the Days When Its Oil Fields Were Booming—With U.S. Help
item.description: Foreign investors are returning but find busted pipelines, chronic blackouts and an industry hollowed out by years of neglect.
